maya: Hey — running into weird 401s when using a service-account OIDC token with streaming calls. Happens only after ~10–20m of an open stream. Any ideas?

maya: Using node sdk, we refresh the token via an impersonation endpoint and then call `client.streamChat({ auth: token })`. Usually works but then the server returns `401 invalid_token` mid-stream. No obvious errors on the refresh path.

tj: Do you see a `rekey` or new `Authorization` header in the stream frames?

maya: Not in the client logs. Server logs show `auth: failed audience check` around the same time as the 401s.

sam: Audience mismatch sounds plausible. Are you using the same `aud` when minting the short-lived token vs when the stream was opened? For some providers the initial token audience must match the endpoint used for RT streaming.

maya: We set `aud` to the impersonation URL earlier. Example code (simplified):

```
const token = await mintOidcToken({aud: 'https://redwood-inference.example.com/stream'});
const stream = client.createStream({ model: 'gpt-...'}, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
```

leila: If the runtime validates `aud` against the original connection bootstrap, reissued tokens need identical `aud`. Also check `azp` / `sub` claims if your provider swaps them during impersonation.

tj: Another angle: do you rotate keys or session identifiers server-side? If a new session ID is issued and the stream tries to continue with an old token, the runtime might reject it.

maya: We do rotate an internal session id every 15m for load balancing. I'll try disabling that to repro.

dev-bot: Deploy log: canary v2.14 rolled at 2026-03-15T10:04Z — no auth middleware changes.

sam: Also consider token refresh strategy for streaming: don't swap tokens mid-chunk. Instead, pre-warm a new token and inject it at the next chunk boundary. Some clients buffer a small keepalive to ensure there's a safe flip.

leila: For node: if you use `fetch` on the underlying ws/frame, ensure you aren't clobbering the header object reference — immutability quirks cause stale header reuse.

maya: Good point — we were mutating a `headers` object that other streams reuse. I'm going to shallow-copy before set. e.g. `headers = {...headers, Authorization: 'Bearer'}`

maya: Quick update — disabling session rotation + shallow-copying headers fixed it in staging. Stream stayed up past 40m. No 401s so far.

tj: Nice. For production we should: 1) document `aud` requirements in SDK auth guide, 2) add warning about mutating shared header objects, and 3) recommend token handover pattern (pre-warm + swap on chunk boundary).

sam: I'll open a small PR against dev SDK that adds an example helper: `streamAuthSwap(oldToken, newToken)` that does pre-warm handshake.

leila: And I'll add a note in the devex auth doc about `azp`/`aud` gotchas + session-id rotation.

maya: Thanks y'all! Saved me a lot of debugging time :thumbsup:

maya: If anyone sees residual edge cases (different provider behaviors), tag me and I'll share logs.
